nodes.summary: For a finite group $G$ and a natural number $p$, the breadth $\operatorname{br}_p(G)$ of $G$ is the maximum of the element breadths $\operatorname{br}_p(g)$ over all $g \in G$.
nodes.title: Breadth of a finite group

nodes.summary: In a finite group $G$, the number of elements of the conjugacy class of any $g \in G$ divides the order $|G|$.
nodes.title: Conjugacy class sizes divide the group order

nodes.summary: In every group, the conjugacy class of the identity element $1$ is the singleton $\{1\}$.
nodes.title: The conjugacy class of the identity

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, $p$ a prime, $k$ a natural number and $g \in G$. If the conjugacy class of $g$ has exactly $p^k$ elements, then the breadth $\operatorname{br}_p(g)$ of $g$ equals $k$.
nodes.title: Breadth from an exact class size

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and $p$ a natural number. For every $g \in G$, the breadth $\operatorname{br}_p(g)$ of $g$ is at most the breadth $\operatorname{br}_p(G)$ of $G$.
nodes.title: Element breadth is at most the group breadth

nodes.summary: In a finite group, the breadth $\operatorname{br}_p(1)$ of the identity element $1$ is $0$ for every natural number $p$.
nodes.title: Breadth of the identity

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, $p$ a natural number and $g \in G$, and write $g^G$ for the conjugacy class of $g$. When $p \ge 2$, the breadth $\operatorname{br}_p(g)$ of $g$ is $\lfloor \log_p |g^G| \rfloor$, the largest natural number $k$ with $p^k \le |g^G|$; when $p \le 1$, it is $0$.
nodes.title: Breadth of an element

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and $p$ a natural number. There is an element $g \in G$ whose breadth $\operatorname{br}_p(g)$ equals the breadth $\operatorname{br}_p(G)$ of $G$.
nodes.title: The group breadth is attained

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $G$ a finite $p$-group. For every $g \in G$ there is a natural number $k$ such that the conjugacy class of $g$ has exactly $p^k$ elements.
nodes.title: Conjugacy classes of a finite $p$-group have $p$-power size

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, $G$ a finite $p$-group and $g \in G$, and write $g^G$ for the conjugacy class of $g$. Then the breadth $\operatorname{br}_p(g)$ of $g$ satisfies $p^{\operatorname{br}_p(g)} = |g^G|$.
nodes.title: Class sizes in a $p$-group via breadth

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
